name: Central Library
features: Makerspace with 3D printers and a sewing table|Ledger Room for local history|Six study rooms, first come|Teen floor|Seed library|Public computers, printing and scanning|Step-free entrance on Mill Street
summary: The 1911 Carnegie building on Kettle Square, with the 1998 glass wing behind it. Home of the Ledger Room, the makerspace and the teen floor.
body:
Central is the oldest and busiest branch: about 1,400 visits on a weekday (story). The reading room in the original Carnegie building still has its oak card catalog, now used as a seed library.

The Ledger Room on the second floor holds the Ossingford Ledger newspaper on microfilm from 1874, city directories, and the county map collection. A local history librarian is on duty Tuesday to Saturday.

name: Millrace Branch
features: Children's reading garden|Laptop lending|Quiet room|Large-print and audiobook wall|Free parking behind the branch
summary: A brick branch beside the old mill race, with a walled reading garden for children and the biggest large-print collection in the system.
body:
Millrace was the town's first branch library, opened in 1952 in a former mill office (story). The children's garden is open whenever the branch is, weather permitting.

Laptops can be borrowed for use inside the branch with a library card.

name: North Quarry Branch
features: Holds pickup locker, open 7 am – 10 pm|Community room for 60|Homework help after school|Spanish-language collection
status_note: Roof work: the reading room is closed until December 11. Holds pickup, returns and the community room stay open.
summary: A 1970s branch in the old quarry neighborhood, with a holds locker outside and a busy after-school homework room.
body: While the roof is replaced, North Quarry has a smaller collection in the community room and staff at a desk by the front door. Holds can still be picked up here, at the desk or from the outdoor locker.

name: Ferrin Heights Branch
features: Recording booth|Board game library|Study rooms|Drive-up returns|Solar roof (story)
summary: The newest branch, opened in 2021 next to Ferrin Heights Middle School, with a recording booth, a board game library and drive-up returns.
body: Ferrin Heights is closed on Mondays and open on Sunday afternoons. The recording booth can be used for podcasts, voice memos and video calls; walk in and ask at the desk.

name: Bookmobile
address: Stops change by day; see the weekly route
features: Holds delivered to any stop|Wheelchair lift|Wi-Fi hotspot at each stop|Large-print and kids' shelves
summary: A 32-foot library on wheels with about 3,000 items, visiting nine stops a week across the county.
body:
Place a hold on anything in the system and choose a Bookmobile stop as your pickup location. The driver-librarians are Ana and Teo (fictional).

If the weather is bad, the Bookmobile posts a route change on the news page by 8 am.
